reflections.summary: Lost because the four brought (Archaludon/Gyarados/Aegislash/Medicham-Mega) were misaligned with the actual opponent core: once Archaludon was burned and Flash Cannon PP was gone, only weak physical Dragon Claw remained against Altaria’s Roost/Moonblast recovery loop, and Medicham-Mega—the correct Mega holder—fell too early to break it. Opponent also revealed they omit Primarina and Gliscor, so the preview over-prepared for absent threats and under-prepared for Altaria stall.
reflections.adjustment: In the next game, replace one slot with a special attacker or Toxic/anti-recovery user that can pressure Altaria through Roost, and do not rely on Archaludon’s Dragon Claw as the sole endgame win condition; also avoid Protect-streak Gyarados against Thunderbolt Gengar-Mega.
reflections.notebook: Opponent durable core: Altaria (Sitrus Berry, Cloud Nine, Roost/Moonblast/Will-O-Wisp/Tailwind) stalls burned physical attackers; Grimmsnarl (Prankster, Light Clay) sets Reflect/Light Screen; Annihilape (Defiant, Expert Belt) punishes drops; Gengar-Mega (Timid, Thunderbolt/Shadow Ball) hits tanks. They consistently do not bring Primarina or Gliscor. Future plan: build the four around special damage and anti-heal/status to break recovery loops; avoid pure physical endgames vulnerable to burn; keep a Mega option but ensure a backup special breaker exists if screens appear.
